content.title: About
content.content: Turtle is a chocolate confection consisting of caramel, nuts (usually walnuts) and a coating of chocolate. It is named for its shape, which resembles a turtle: the "shell" is the chocolate and the "body" is the caramel‑nut filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The turtle candy originated in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became a staple in coffee shops and bakeries.
Traditional recipes use walnuts, but variations with almonds, pecans or cashews are also common.
The combination of sweet caramel, crunchy nuts and bitter chocolate is considered a perfect flavor balance.
In some countries turtles are sold as small bite‑size bars, while in others they are made as larger pieces that are sliced into portions.
Turtles are often used as decorative elements for cakes and desserts.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: The nuts provide monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Chocolate is rich in flavonoids, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Walnuts supply magnesium, phosphorus and copper.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The mix of sugar and fat delivers a quick source of energy, making it a convenient small snack.

items.title: Vitamin E source
items.content: Nuts in the turtle provide vitamin E, an antioxidant that supports cell membranes.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: Turtles contain nuts that can trigger severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The candy is rich in sugar, which can contribute to dental caries and affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Turtles are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑management diets.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: The chocolate coating contains saturated fat, which should be limited in heart‑related conditions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Turtles can be enjoyed as a standalone treat, added to ice cream, used in baking, or as a garnish for cakes. For a softer texture, gently warm them in the microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store turtles in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, keep them refrigerated to prevent the chocolate from melting.
